comments.note: ElementTest.php achieves perfect 1:1 assertion coverage: 63 PHPUnit assertions vs 63 active assert() calls in element_testcase.php.

ReaderElementTest.php has 46 assertions vs 49 active in reader/element_testcase.php. The 3-count gap is legitimate: lines 59-60 (malformed table, 2 asserts) were correctly omitted because the reader library auto-appended </tr> but the main library does not — making those assertions impossible to satisfy against str_get_html(). Lines 94-95 are exact duplicates of lines 52-53 (same table, same assertions) and their omission is correct. The developer's comment 'reader had these commented out' is factually wrong but the decision was right.
str_get_dom() is referenced only in a header comment confirming its replacement: no actual str_get_dom() call exists in test code. AC4 verified.

summary: Code review of tests/DOM/ElementTest.php and tests/DOM/ReaderElementTest.php. Both files are well-structured and follow the project's established PHPUnit patterns. Adaptation from reader library (str_get_dom → str_get_html) is well-documented. No blocking issues. Three low-priority non-blocking observations recorded.

comments.note: ElementTest.php::testOutertextList — the final block appends a full well-formed table round-trip assertion identical to testOutertextTable. Pure duplication from a direct source port. No harm but wastes execution time and will confuse future maintainers. Consider removing or adding a comment explaining why it's repeated.

ReaderElementTest.php has no setUp()/tearDown() — all $dom instances are local variables cleared manually at method end. If an assertion fails before $dom->clear() is reached, the DOM object is never freed. All other test classes in tests/DOM/ guard against this via tearDown(). Mitigation: convert to $this->dom class property with tearDown() in a future cleanup.

ElementTest.php::testReplacement — $es[0]->class is assigned 'class_test' twice in sequence with only the isset assertion in between. The second assignment is a no-op (same value). This is a direct artifact of the source testcase where the first assignment was the target of a separate assert(). Harmless but slightly confusing to read.
